newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 25.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Financial Express
CABINET ADOPTS BUDGET IN TOTO

The Cabinet has adopted the budget presented by former finance minister P. Chidambaram in toto and decided to pursue it in parliament. The Cabinet was of the view that the budget and the Finance Bill were the property of parliament and could not tampered with.
PEUGEOT MAY BUY OUT PAL STAKE IN JOINT VENTURE

Peugeot plans to buy out the Doshi's stake in the Pal-Peugeot joint venture with funds from the sale of its 2.8 percent stake in Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M), which fetched around 950 million rupees. M&M's promoters' stake in the company increased to over 30 percent with this purchase. Peugeot would use the amount to either buy out the 31.7 per cent stake of their partners in PAL-Peugeot, which reeled under a 920 million rupee loss during the last fiscal year, or recapitalise losses of an equivalent amount.
The Times Of India
TAMIL MAANILA CONGRESS MAY JOIN GOVERNMENT

Prospects of the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) joining the United Front government appear to have brightened. The TMC party executive was scheduled to meet on April 27 to take a final decision, sources said. They added that the pressure of senior government functionaries, including the prime minister, was beginning to have some impact on the rank and file of the party. Apart from that, there was pressure from industry on the TMC to rejoin the government so that P. Chidambaram could become finance minister once again.
The Hindustan Times
100,000 RUPEE PAYMENT TO MECCA FIRE VICTIMS' RELATIVES

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral has set up a four-member team to examine the causes of the fire near Mecca. The committee would also verifiy whether Saudi guides shut the camp gates which prevented Haj pilgrims from fleeing to safety. He also announced an ex gratia payment of 100,000 rupees to the next of kin of those pilgrims killed.
Indian Express
CHAOS IN UP HOUSE, 28 LAWMAKERS EXPELLED

The speaker of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly has expelled 28 Samajwadi Party members, including the leader of the opposition, for misconduct. The legislators turned unruly after a remark by the chief minister while replying to the charge that legislators were not being consulted in finalising developmental schemes.
The Economic Times
RBI PEGS GENERAL REFINANCE AT 44.6 BLN RUPEES

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has fixed an overall limit of 44.599 billion rupees under its general refinance facility (GRF) for 98 scheduled commercial banks. The facility was announced in the monetary policy for the first half of 1997/98 (April-March). The RBI also fixed individual limits for these banks.
GILTS LOSE ON PANIC OVER SALE OF 50 BLN RUPEE 10-YEAR PAPER

Prices of government securities dropped across the board by 0.5-0.6 rupees in the gilts market on uncertainty over the impact of a 50 billion rupee private placement of 10-year paper with the RBI. However, much of the initial panic subsided as the security was not put on sale by the RBI, alleviating fears that money would be sucked out of the system immediately.
TERM MONEY MARKET SIGNALS NEW INTER BANK RATE

The money market has thrown up some indicative rates and quotes for term deposits. At the same time, bankers were holding consultations on what it would take to develop a Mumbai Inter-Bank Offered Rate (Mibor) market. A meeting was held between some large banks to work out modalities of how the system should work. The Indian financial system was on the threshold of witnessing its first ever term money market, which would hopefully give rise to Mibor, on the lines of Libor.
TELECOMMUNICATIONS FIRMS AGREE TO SCALE DOWN PRICES

Global telecommunications firms have agreed to slash equipment prices for 1.3 million telephone lines by more than 20 percent. Earlier, the Communications Ministry had rejected the rates quoted by these companies for a global tender. The equipment could not be delivered in 1996/97, when it was originally scheduled to be installed. Department of Telecom officials confirmed the six companies -- AT&T, Alcatel, Siemens, Fujitsu, Ericsson and NEC -- had indicated they were scaling down their quotation.
Financial Express
NINE STATE FIRMS WANT FREEDOM TO MAKE INVESTMENT DECISIONS

The nine state-owned companies that were assured greater autonomy in the budget have asked for the delegation of complete control over investment decisions. They recommended the government abolish any ceiling on investment and asked to be kept beyond the purview of the Comptroller and Auditor General, the Committee on Public Undertakings and other parliamentary committes.
OIL & NATURAL GAS CORP PROJECTS FALL IN NET PROFIT

The Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has forecast a 28 percent fall in its net profit and a production shortfall close to one million tonnes in financial 1997/98 (March-April). Sales would go up only marginally this year to 134.92 billion rupees against 132 billion in the previous year. ONGC projected a 19.75 billion rupee profit after tax in 1996/97, but projected a fall of 14.23 billion rupees in net in 1997/98.
Business Standard
PRIME CORPORATES' BORROWING COST PLUNGES 150 BASIS POINTS

The borrowing cost of prime corporates has fallen by more than 150 basis points in the previous week. This was a direct fallout of the freedom given to banks in making lending decisions in the credit policy this year. Virtually all top-rated corporates, as well as many multinationals, were looking to place 18-month debentures with banks priced in the 14.5-15 percent range. It indicated short term money for companies became cheaper compared to the rates a month ago. There were also indications that funds for longer tenures were likely to cost less by at least 150-200 basis points.
FARM MINISTRY ACCEPTS IMPORT CURBS PHASEOUT

The agriculture ministry has recommended a phaseout period for import curbs on various agricultural commodities, varying from over one to five years. India was unable to submit a phaseout period for its quantitative restrictions on imports in January, due to objections by the agriculture minister. Meanwhile, various countries including Australia, Japan and the United States were conducting bilateral negotiations with India on the issue of removal of quantitative restrictions.
PRIVATE SECTOR MAY INVEST 7.15 BLN RUPEES IN AIRPORTS

The Airports Authority of India (AAI) expects the private sector to invest 7.15 billion rupees in the airport sector through the build-operate-transfer mechanism. It also plans to raise 4.5 million rupees through a public issue of bonds. This would be part of the AAI's ninth plan targets. AAI expects to generate 20 billion rupees internally over the next five years. It also plans to raise 750 million rupees in commercial borrowings in the domestic as well as overseas market.
ERNST & YOUNG FORECAST SIX PCT GDP GROWTH IN 1997/98

Ernst & Young forecast a six percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth for fiscial 1997/98 (April-March), the same as the previous year. The global management consultant warned of continuing political instability in the country affecting business and foreign investor confidence. It expected real interest rates to remain high during 1997/98. However, industrial growth was estimated to rise marginally to 8.5 percent from eight percent during the year to March 1998, powered primarily by the light manufacturing sector, which does not have heavy power usage.
VIDEOCON PLANS PETROCHEMICALS FORAY

The Videocon group is planning to enter the petrochemicals sector through a separate company called Videocon Karnataka Petrochemicais. The group was negotiating with Samsung and Mitsubishi Corporation for their equity participation in the proposed joint venture company. It was also conducting a feasibility study for the petrochemical unit to be set up at Mangalore in Karnataka. The project cost was estimated at 48 billion rupees.
Business Line
RELIANCE TO FOCUS ON WORLD-SCALE PLANTS

Reliance Industries plans to enhance its presence in the oil sector by picking up equity overseas through the purchase of oil and gas assets and production sharing contracts. The firm said its investments in the Panna, Mukta and Tapti oilfields would be in the range of $350 million over a period of five years. The company's corporate strategy would centre around building world-scale plants, focusing on the domestic market, implementing vertical backward integration, maintaining its competitive cost positions and leveraging core competencies.
